faq.q: How do you connect an ammeter?
faq.a: In series, right in the loop, so that all the current has to flow through it. An ammeter has almost no resistance, so it does not slow the current it is measuring.
asks: Why is an ammeter in series?

faq.q: How do you connect a voltmeter?
faq.a: In parallel, across the part you are testing, with one lead on each side. It measures the voltage drop, the energy each bit of charge gives up in that part.
asks: Why is a voltmeter in parallel?

faq.q: What can you work out from the two readings?
faq.a: Multiply volts by amps to get the power in watts, or divide volts by amps to get the resistance in ohms. With 6 volts and 2 amps, the bulb uses 12 watts and has 3 ohms resistance.
asks: How do you find resistance from a meter?

faq.a: A multimeter is one meter that can be switched to measure volts, amps or ohms. You turn the dial and plug the leads into the right sockets for each job.
asks: How do I use a multimeter?

faq.q: What happens if you connect an ammeter across a part?
faq.a: An ammeter has almost no resistance, so across a part it makes a short cut for the current. A big current can flow, which may blow the meter's fuse or drain the battery fast.
asks: Why must an ammeter not go in parallel?

facts: An ideal ammeter has zero resistance and an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance.
Digital multimeters can measure volts, amps and ohms with one instrument.
